Question
========
An AI assistant can write R code for you. Given that, why does it still matter that you
understand what R and RStudio each do?

Answerlist
----------
* Because you still need a working installation to run any code, and you're the one who has to recognize and fix problems when the setup breaks.
* It doesn't matter anymore; once AI can write code, installation and setup knowledge is obsolete.
* Because AI assistants cannot generate R code unless RStudio is installed first.
* Because open-source software requires you to personally rewrite its source code before use.

Solution
========
AI tools can generate code, but they don't install software, manage your files, or debug a broken
local setup for you. You still need a working R/RStudio installation, and you need to be able to
tell which part of the system (R, RStudio, or a package) is causing a problem.

Answerlist
----------
* Correct
* Wrong: someone (or something) still needs a working R/RStudio setup to actually run code, and problems still need to be diagnosed by a person.
* Wrong: AI assistants can write R code regardless of whether RStudio is installed; RStudio is a convenience for you, not a requirement for code generation.
* Wrong: open source means the code is available to inspect and modify if you want to, not that you are required to rewrite it.
